ga_beam_me_up_scotty_area_2.blurb: A cluster of granite boulders inside the Boat Rock bouldering park on the west side of Atlanta, set just beyond the lake. The 24 problems here run from VB up to the double digits, though the bulk sit between V0 and V6, so there is something for beginners and for strong climbers alike. The mix is varied: slabs, cracks, aretes and seams on textured granite, with a couple of easy trad lines tucked among them. Several of the easier problems earn top ratings, which makes this a good stop for a relaxed session. Surrounded by suburban housing, it feels more like a neighborhood park than a wilderness crag.

ga_land_of_aretes.blurb: A group of tall boulders of mixed quality in the forest of the Zahnd bouldering area on Lookout Mountain, in the far northwest corner of Georgia. Nearly all of the 24 lines are boulder problems, with a few trad lines mixed in. Grades spread widely: a handful of easy V0 to V3 problems that make good warm-ups, a middle group around V5 to V7, and a few hard testpieces reaching V10. The namesake arete lines are the draw, and the boulders are grey and often pebbly. The setting is quiet and rural, and the walk from the lot goes past the Middle Blocs.
ga_land_of_aretes.approach: From the parking lot, take the left fork of the trail and keep going past the Middle Blocs.

ga_campus_punks.blurb: A corridor of boulders within Rocktown, the sandstone maze on Pigeon Mountain near LaFayette in northwest Georgia. Climbs line both sides, with slabs on one wall and steeper faces on the other. There are 23 problems, mostly V0 to V6, with a handful of easy ones for warming up, a solid middle of V2 to V5 problems, and a single very hard line near the top of the scale. It sits on the trail running between the Orb and Tao areas and the Bads, so it is easy to fold into a longer circuit around the field. Rocktown sandstone offers slopers, crimps and rails with committing top-outs.

ga_hueco_simulator.blurb: A long wall of sandstone boulders at Rocktown, on Pigeon Mountain in northwest Georgia, a little beyond the midpoint of the Upper Maze section. The 22 problems are friendly: plenty of VB to V3 climbing on a roughly 20-foot overhang covered in jugs, slopers and flakes, plus a few harder lines up to V8. The walls are large and somewhat steep, making it a popular warm-up zone for all levels. The boulders take a lot of sun, so it suits cooler spring days best.

ga_main_slab_wall_area.blurb: The main friction cliff on Currahee Mountain near Toccoa in northeast Georgia, climbing granitic gneiss slab. Of the 22 routes, most are trad, with a good number of bolted lines and one top-rope option. Grades lean toward 5.10, with a scattering of 5.6 to 5.9 routes for newer leaders and a few 5.11 and 5.12 lines at the top. Bolting can be sparse, so some trad gear is useful on many lines. Most of the rock sees sun through the day, especially in summer, though much of the landing zone sits in shade. It is also considered good practice for friction climbing in the Carolinas.

ga_brick_wall_climbs.blurb: The steepest and shortest wall on Currahee Mountain near Toccoa in northeast Georgia, on granitic gneiss. Of the 20 routes, a dozen are sport, seven are trad and one is a boulder problem, and the grades start at 5.9 with the bulk at 5.10 to 5.12. Most lines are bolted and can be top-roped, and the wall is heavily featured. It faces west and takes only afternoon sun, so it stays shaded for much of the day and works well on warm days. A beginner wall it is not, since nothing here is below 5.9.
